requirement: Create a POST /transfers endpoint with TransferRequest, DomainException hierarchy (InsufficientFundsException 402, AccountNotFoundException 404), RFC error envelope with details and request_id, X-Request-ID header tracing, and balance check.
skeleton: FastAPI route with custom exception handlers, RFC error envelope, X-Request-ID propagation, and account balance validation.
caption: A FastAPI transfer service with an in-memory account ledger and a domain exception hierarchy translated into a uniform JSON error envelope. TransferRequest is a pydantic model with from_account and to_account of at least one character and an amount strictly greater than zero, so a zero or negative amount fails validation with 422. DomainException extends Exception and stores message, a code defaulting to DOMAIN_ERROR, and a details dict defaulting to empty; InsufficientFundsException fixes the code INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, and AccountNotFoundException fixes ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. ACCOUNTS_DB maps acc_1, acc_2, and acc_3 to balances of 100.0, 50.0, and 0.0, and reset_db restores that mapping. Two handlers registered with app.exception_handler build the envelope: each reads the incoming X-Request-ID header, or generates a uuid4 string when absent, and returns a JSONResponse whose body is an error object with code, message, details, and request_id, with the same id echoed in an X-Request-ID response header. The InsufficientFundsException handler answers 402 and the AccountNotFoundException handler answers 404. POST /transfers declares status 200; it raises AccountNotFoundException with the account id in details when either account is unknown, and raises InsufficientFundsException with available, requested, and shortfall in details when the current balance is less than the amount, so a transfer that drains the balance to exactly zero is allowed. On success it debits the sender, credits the receiver, and returns a completed status with the amount, the remaining balance, and the request id. GET /accounts/{account_id} returns the balance or raises AccountNotFoundException.

rationale.teaches: Domain exceptions mapped to a JSONResponse with the right status, a stable error envelope including details and request_id, and X-Request-ID propagated from the request to the response header.
rationale.why: A handler that returns a plain dict or a 200 still produces valid JSON, so a body-only check passes. The oracle reads status, body shape, and response headers together, which is what the generator must assemble.

candidates.why_wrong: Insufficient funds answers 200 OK, so the client treats a rejected transfer as successful.
The details field is dropped from the envelope, so the client never learns which balance or amount failed.
The handler returns a bare dict, so the response status collapses to 200 and the X-Request-ID header is never set.
The incoming X-Request-ID header is ignored and a fresh uuid is generated, so the caller's trace id never appears in the error.
A transfer that would leave exactly zero balance is rejected as insufficient funds.
